title: Kickstarter for iOS
description: Build a SwiftUI crowdfunding discovery demo with local project search, detail views, save/back workflows, validation, and local state persistence.
problem: Learners need a source-grounded way to understand and extend Kickstarter for iOS while separating implemented behavior from demo data, simulations, and missing integrations.
audience: Third-year undergraduate students who have completed introductory programming and want a practical mobile mini-project.
prerequisites: Git basics and ability to run the platform tooling described in the source README
learning_outcomes: Explain and trace project fields, computed progress, identity, and sample catalogue in its named source files.
Explain and trace category data, search matching, sort ordering, and discovery rendering in its named source files.
Explain and trace pledge validation, status changes, detail state, and progress display in its named source files.
Explain and trace projectstore, userdefaults keys, toggling, and backed/saved projections in its named source files.
Explain and trace environment object injection, navigationstack, and view actions in its named source files.
Explain and trace core rule tests, temporary userdefaults, target generation, and simulator checklist in its named source files.
Distinguish unit-test evidence from device, service, and deployment evidence.
Propose a safe, bounded extension without describing it as already implemented.
